'''Susan Mary Rees''' (born 31 July 1953<ref>GRO Register of Births: SEP 1953 4a 294 CAMBRIDGE – Susan M. Rees, mmn = Cushen</ref>) is a British [[mathematician]] and an emeritus professor of mathematics at the [[University of Liverpool]] since 2018, specialising in research in [[complex dynamical system]]s.<ref>[http://tulip.liv.ac.uk/portal/pls/portal/tulwwwmerge.mergepage?p_template=rae_staff_mf&p_tulipproc=raestaff&p_params=%3Fp_func%3DSDMF%26p_select%3DRAE%26p_hash%3DA679765%26p_url%3D122%26p_template%3Drae_staff_mf Mary Rees profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100123230121/http://tulip.liv.ac.uk/portal/pls/portal/tulwwwmerge.mergepage?p_template=rae_staff_mf&p_tulipproc=raestaff&p_params=%3Fp_func%3DSDMF%26p_select%3DRAE%26p_hash%3DA679765%26p_url%3D122%26p_template%3Drae_staff_mf |date=23 January 2010 }}, [[University of Liverpool]]</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.liv.ac.uk/~maryrees/maryrees.homepage.html |title=Dr. Mary Rees |publisher= University of Liverpool |date=2008-01-18 |access-date=2014-01-02}}</ref>

== Career ==
Rees was born in [[Cambridge]]. After obtaining her BA in 1974 and MSc in 1975 at [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]], she did research in mathematics under the direction of [[Bill Parry (mathematician)|Bill Parry]] at the [[University of Warwick]], obtaining a PhD in 1978.  Her first postdoctoral position was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1978 to 1979. Later she worked at [[Institut des hautes études scientifiques]] and the [[University of Minnesota]]. Following this she worked at the [[University of Liverpool]] until her retirement. She became professor of mathematics in 2002 and retired in 2018, becoming an emeritus professor.

She was awarded a [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 1988. The citation<ref>Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 20 (1988), no. 6, p. 639.</ref> notes that, in particular,<blockquote>
Her most spectacular theorem<ref>Positive measure sets of [[ergodic]] [[rational map]]s, ''Ann. Sci. École Norm. Sup''. 19 (1986), no. 3, 383–407.</ref> has been to show that in the space of [[rational map]]s of the [[Riemann sphere]] of degree ''d''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;2 those maps that are [[Ergodicity|ergodic]] with respect to [[Lebesgue measure]] and leave invariant an [[absolutely continuous]] [[probability measure]] form a set of positive measure.</blockquote>

She also spoke at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] at [[Kyoto]] in 1990.<ref name="ewm">{{cite web|last1=EWM|url=http://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/mary-rees|title=Mary Reese|website=European Women in Mathematics|access-date=25 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616030743/http://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/mary-rees|archive-date=16 June 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>  In recent years, much of Rees' work has focused on the dynamics of quadratic rational maps; i.e. rational maps of the Riemann sphere of degree two, including an extensive monograph.<ref>Views of parameter space: Topographer and resident, Asterisque 288 (2003)</ref> In 2004, she also presented an alternative proof of the [[Ending lamination theorem|Ending Laminations Conjecture]] of [[William Thurston|Thurston]],<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0404007 The Ending Laminations Theorem direct from Teichmüller geodesics], Preprint, 2004</ref> which had been proved by Brock, [[Richard Canary|Canary]] and [[Yair Minsky|Minsky]] shortly before.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0412006 The classification of Kleinian surface groups, II: The Ending Lamination Conjecture], Preprint, 2004</ref>

==FRS==
She was elected to a [[List of fellows of the Royal Society P, Q, R#R|Fellowship]] of the [[Royal Society]] in 2002.

==Family==
Her father [[David Rees (mathematician)|David Rees]] was also a distinguished mathematician, who worked on [[Enigma machine|Enigma]] in [[Hut 6]] at [[Bletchley Park]].  Her sister [[Sarah Rees (professor)|Sarah Rees]] is also a mathematician.<ref name="ewm"/>

==Works==
* Mary Rees (2010) "Multiple equivalent matings with the aeroplane polynomial". ''Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems'', pp.&nbsp;20
* Mary Rees (2008) "William Parry FRS 1934–2006". ''Biographical Memoirs of the Royal Society'', 54, pp.&nbsp;229–243
* Mary Rees (2004) "Teichmuller distance is not $C^{2+\varepsilon }$". ''Proc London Math'', 88, pp.&nbsp;114–134
* Mary Rees (2003) "Views of Parameter Space: Topographer and Resident". ''[[Astérisque|Asterisque]]'', 288, pp.&nbsp;1–418
* Mary Rees (2002) "Teichmuller distance for analytically finite surfaces is $C^{2}$." ''Proc. London Math. Soc''. 85 (2002) 686 – 716.,85, pp.&nbsp;686–716
